evidence.match_text: Activation of the Incident Command System

evidence.text: Activation may begin with a notification, emergency code announcement, leadership assessment, command center activation, or immediate protective action. The person activating the plan should consider the seriousness of the event, expected duration, resident impact, staffing capacity, communications needs, outside-agency coordination, and whether the incident may escalate.

Activation may begin with a notification, emergency code announcement, leadership assessment, command center activation, or immediate protective action. The person activating the plan should consider the seriousness of the event, expected duration, resident impact, staffing capacity, communications needs, outside-agency coordination, and whether the incident may escalate.

The activating leader or Incident Commander should make or delegate notifications based on the type and severity of the event. Notifications may include internal leadership, department heads, direct-care staff, residents or representatives when appropriate, emergency response agencies, emergency management, regulatory contacts, vendors, receiving partners, or other support organizations.

evidence.text: The directory should help the command center, resident placement staff, transportation coordinators, and resident-care leaders identify potential receiving locations, confirm contact methods, understand agreement status, and estimate available capacity during partial or full evacuation.

The chart is not intended to show every possible person working in an emergency. It shows the command roles that may be activated and the relationships between them. The Incident Commander may scale the structure up or down based on the incident.
